prompt.context: Our client is an online dating startup named Grad-U-Date, which specializes in matching graduate students with other graduate students. Grad-U-Date has finished building their website and are now looking for your assistance in deciding on a strategy to monetize their website.
prompt.question: What is Grad-U-Date's best method of monetization? How profitable will the company be?

clarifying_info.q: What is the gender ratio of users?
Which students are considered professional students?
clarifying_info.a: MBA, law, and medical students are considered professional students.

clarifying_info.q: Has the website already been built? Are website development costs a factor?
clarifying_info.a: The website has already been built and is considered a sunk cost.
Grad-U-Date will only operate within the United States.
There are 4 major competitors and hundreds of small competitors. There are currently no other online dating services that focus only on graduate students.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any market trends to be aware of?
clarifying_info.a: There has been a significant increase in the number of free dating phone apps starting in late 2012.

clarifying_info.q: Can the company use multiple revenue models?
clarifying_info.a: Only one revenue model can be used.

exhibits.title: Student Enrolment Information
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing new graduate students per university per year by type, plus the number of years for each degree program. There is also a note about the total number of universities in the US.

exhibits.title: Product Usage
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the forecasted percentage of graduate students using Grad-U-Date under each of three revenue models, plus pricing details for each model.

exhibits.title: Online Dating Market Trends
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis line chart showing trends from 2008 to 2014 in the percentage of users paying a monthly fee and the average monthly fee charged across the online dating market.

data.trend: Both metrics show a declining trend, with a notable acceleration in decline starting around 2012-2013

framework: Market sizing: estimate the total addressable market (number of grad students in the US)
Competitive landscape: assess market structure, existing competitors, and differentiation opportunities
Monetization models: identify possible revenue models and pros/cons of each
Profitability analysis: calculate revenue and profit under each viable model given fixed and variable costs
Recommendation: select the model with the highest sustainable profit and defend against risks

questions.prompt: What types of monetization models could Grad-U-Date use? What are the advantages and disadvantages of each?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate brainstorms at least 3 models and ideally 5+. Models include: Monthly Fee (predictable revenue, but shrinking market); Advertising (large user base, low per-user revenue); Premium Account / Freemium (free tier drives adoption, paid tier monetizes power users); Profile Consulting Services (high margin, niche); Micro-transactions such as pay-per-message or profile bump (usage-based, can scale). Candidate should note that only one model can be chosen.

questions.prompt: Grad-U-Date is considering limiting the site to only MBA students. What issues might there be with an MBA-only dating website?
questions.guidance: There are more men than women at most MBA programs, causing a significant gender skew. Limiting to MBA students unnecessarily restricts the market size. Most MBA students tend to be older than other graduate students, so many may already be married or in a committed relationship.

questions.prompt: What is the potential market size for Grad-U-Date? (Use Exhibit 1.)
questions.guidance: Estimate total grad students currently enrolled in the US by multiplying new enrollees per year by program length, then multiply by number of universities.

math.setup: Total students at one university = (new per year) x (years in program) for each type, summed. Then multiply by 1,000 universities.
steps: Medical: 450 new/yr x 4 years = 1,800 students per university
MBA: 300 new/yr x 2 years = 600 students per university
Law: 200 new/yr x 3 years = 600 students per university
Non-professional: 1,000 new/yr x 3 years = 3,000 students per university
Market size: 6,000 x 1,000 universities = 6,000,000 graduate students

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit of each revenue model. Fixed costs are $10,000,000 per year and variable operating cost is $1 per member per year. Which revenue model would you recommend? (Use Exhibit 2.)
questions.guidance: Use the forecasted user percentages and pricing details from Exhibit 2 to calculate customers, revenue, and profit for each model. The monthly fee model yields the highest profit.

math.setup: For each model: Customers = 6,000,000 x forecasted %; Revenue = Customers x price x 12 months (adjusted for mix where applicable); Profit = Revenue - $10,000,000 fixed costs - (Customers x $1 variable cost).
steps: Profit ranking: Monthly Fee $25.7M > Premium Account $20.6M > Advertising $16.4M
math.answer: Monthly Fee model yields the highest profit at $25,700,000; Premium Account is second at $20,600,000; Advertising is third at $16,400,000.

questions.prompt: Does the information in Exhibit 3 change your recommendation for which revenue model?
questions.guidance: Candidate should switch recommendation from monthly fee to premium account. Exhibit 3 shows that both the percentage of users willing to pay a monthly fee and the average monthly fee have been rapidly declining since 2008, with acceleration after 2012. It is therefore unlikely that the 5% forecasted uptake or $10 fee assumed in the monthly fee model can be sustained, making its projected profitability unreliable going forward.

questions.prompt: Why do you think that the percentage of users paying monthly fees dropped so quickly starting in 2013?
questions.guidance: Key reasons: increased competition in the online dating market; high-quality free dating apps were released that are more convenient (Tinder launched in late 2012); users have a free alternative so willingness to pay a subscription fee decreases sharply.

questions.prompt: Given your recommended revenue model (premium account), what other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure ideas into two buckets: reduce costs and increase revenue. Strong candidates organize their brainstorm rather than listing items randomly.

brainstorming.prompt: Given the premium account revenue model, what other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit?

categories.name: Reduce Costs
ideas: Outsource servers to lower infrastructure costs
Provide only email support and remove phone support to cut staffing costs

categories.name: Increase Revenue
ideas: Create a mobile app to attract more users
Partner with popular date locations for deals and referral revenue
Expand eligibility to recent graduate school alumni
Add micro-transactions such as paying to boost profile traffic visibility
Incorporate social media integration to grow user base
Explore whether premium accounts and advertising can be combined

recommendation: Grad-U-Date should adopt the premium account revenue model

The monthly fee model, despite showing the highest current-period profit ($25.7M), should not be selected because market data shows that the share of users willing to pay monthly fees is rapidly declining due to competitive pressure from free apps such as Tinder
The premium account model is expected to generate $20,600,000 in annual profit and is more resilient to the trend away from subscription fees
risks: Premium account adoption could also be declining, similar to the monthly fee segment
A smaller percentage of users than the forecasted 30% may purchase premium accounts
The ad-supported model could be growing faster than the premium account model
Graduate students may not have sufficient disposable income to purchase premium accounts
The number of people enrolling in graduate school could decrease, shrinking the market
Graduate students may be unwilling to limit their dating pool to other graduate students
next_steps: Explore building a mobile app to capture users migrating to phone-based dating
Research market trends for ad-supported and premium account revenue models to validate projections
Consider expanding into adjacent markets such as undergraduates or other countries
Launch additional revenue streams: profile consulting services and date location deals
Add micro-transactions such as profile traffic boosts
Evaluate whether premium accounts and advertising can be combined without cannibalizing each other
Incorporate social media integration to grow user acquisition
